claim: Sudden cardiac death (SCD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide and is responsible for up to 20% of all deaths in the USA.
source: Sudden cardiac death (SCD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide and is responsible for up to 20% of all deaths in the USA (Benjamin et al., 2019; Deo and Albert, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Benjamin et al., 2019; Deo and Albert, 2012).

claim: The incidence of SCD increases exponentially with age.
source: The incidence of SCD increases exponentially with age, which poses a growing problem as the portion of the US population 65 years or older is estimated to increase to 15% by 2030 (Benjamin et al., 2019; Partridge et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Benjamin et al., 2019; Partridge et al., 2018).

claim: The portion of the US population 65 years or older is estimated to increase to 15% by 2030.
source: The incidence of SCD increases exponentially with age, which poses a growing problem as the portion of the US population 65 years or older is estimated to increase to 15% by 2030 (Benjamin et al., 2019; Partridge et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Benjamin et al., 2019; Partridge et al., 2018).

claim: The vast majority of SCDs are caused by ventricular tachycardia/ventricular fibrillation (VT/VF) subsequent to myocardial infarction (MI).
source: The vast majority of SCDs are caused by ventricular tachycardia/ventricular fibrillation (VT/VF) subsequent to myocardial infarction (MI) (Kolettis, 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Kolettis, 2013).

claim: Progressive tissue remodeling in the days-to-years post-MI can establish a substrate and trigger for potentially lethal arrhythmias.
source: Immediate clinical reperfusion interventions can limit the extent of acute ischemic injury and acute arrhythmic mortality post-MI, however progressive tissue remodeling in the days-to-years post-MI can establish a substrate and trigger for potentially lethal arrhythmias (Mendonca Costa et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Mendonca Costa et al., 2018).

claim: The tissue remodeling process post-MI is well described in young animals.
source: This tissue remodeling process is well described in young animals (van den Borne et al., 2010), but less is known about what changes to this process occur with age and how these changes increase risk of arrhythmia initiation and propagation.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (van den Borne et al., 2010).

claim: The aging rabbit heart recapitulates cardiac dysfunctions observed in aging humans, including aortic stiffening, reduced ventricular compliance, increased interstitial fibrosis, abnormal conduction in the His-Purkinje system, and lower thresholds for induced ventricular arrhythmias.
source: We showed that the aging rabbit heart recapitulates cardiac dysfunctions observed in aging humans, including aortic stiffening, reduced ventricular compliance, increased interstitial fibrosis, abnormal conduction in the His-Purkinje system, and lower thresholds for induced ventricular arrhythmias (Cooper et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work (Cooper et al., 2012).

claim: Aged rabbit myocytes exhibit defects in autophagy and mitochondrial function resulting in increased mitochondrial reactive oxygen species which oxidized the ryanodine receptor and promoted spontaneous Ca2+ release.
source: We also demonstrated defects in autophagy and mitochondrial function in isolated aged rabbit myocytes resulting in increased mitochondrial reactive oxygen species which oxidized the ryanodine receptor and promoted spontaneous Ca2+ release (Cooper et al., 2013; Murphy et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to the authors' previous work (Cooper et al., 2013; Murphy et al., 2019).

claim: Infarction by embolic coil occlusion results in electrophysiological remodeling characteristic of human MI, including functional reentry anchored at the infarct border zone (IBZ), reduction in ejection fraction, and lower thresholds for monomorphic VT induced by programmed stimulation.
source: Infarction by this method results in electrophysiological remodeling characteristic of human MI, including functional reentry anchored at the infarct border zone (IBZ), reduction in ejection fraction, and lower thresholds for monomorphic VT induced by programmed stimulation (Morrissey et al., 2017; Ziv et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Morrissey et al., 2017; Ziv et al., 2012).

claim: Cellular senescence is a stress response characterized by irreversible proliferation arrest, resistance to apoptosis, and secretion of a collection of inflammatory cytokines, growth factors, and proteases termed the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP).
source: Cellular senescence is a stress response characterized by irreversible proliferation arrest, resistance to apoptosis, and secretion of a collection of inflammatory cytokines, growth factors, and proteases termed the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) (Coppé et al., 2010; Rodier et al., 2009; Campisi and Robert, 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Coppé et al., 2010; Rodier et al., 2009; Campisi and Robert, 2014).

claim: Transient senescence plays beneficial roles in young animals in wound healing by limiting fibrosis, in tumor suppression, and in development.
source: Transient senescence plays beneficial roles in young animals in wound healing by limiting fibrosis, in tumor suppression, and in development (Wang et al., 2011; Storer et al., 2013; Demaria et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Wang et al., 2011; Storer et al., 2013; Demaria et al., 2014).

claim: Senescent cells accumulate with age in many tissues and accelerate many aging-associated pathologies in a paracrine manner via SASP-mediated chronic inflammatory signaling and/or in a juxtacrine manner via transfer of intracellular proteins to neighboring cells.
source: However, senescent cells accumulate with age in many tissues and accelerate many aging-associated pathologies in a paracrine manner via SASP-mediated chronic inflammatory signaling and/or in a juxtacrine manner via transfer of intracellular proteins to neighboring cells (Prata et al., 2018; Vicente et al., 2016; Burton and Krizhanovsky, 2014; Shibamoto et al., 2019; Kirschner et al., 2020; Biran et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Prata et al., 2018; Vicente et al., 2016; Burton and Krizhanovsky, 2014; Shibamoto et al., 2019; Kirschner et al., 2020; Biran et al., 2015).

claim: Genetic or pharmacological elimination of senescent cells with age slows the onset and progression of many aging pathologies, including atherosclerosis, diabetes, idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, osteoarthritis, and neurodegenerative diseases.
source: Genetic or pharmacological elimination of senescent cells with age slows the onset and progression of many aging pathologies, including atherosclerosis, diabetes, idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, osteoarthritis, and neurodegenerative diseases (Baker et al., 2016; Baker et al., 2011; Childs et al., 2015; Zhu et al., 2015; Chang et al., 2016; Kim and Kim, 2019; Kirkland et al., 2017; van Deursen, 2019; Kirkland and Tchkonia, 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Baker et al., 2016; Baker et al., 2011; Childs et al., 2015; Zhu et al., 2015; Chang et al., 2016; Kim and Kim, 2019; Kirkland et al., 2017; van Deursen, 2019; Kirkland and Tchkonia, 2017).

claim: In the adult infarcted wild-type mouse heart, senescent cells arise in the scar and IBZ around day 3 post-MI and are largely cleared by day 7.
source: In the adult infarcted wild-type mouse heart, senescent cells arise in the scar and IBZ around day 3 post-MI and are largely cleared by day 7 (Shibamoto et al., 2019; Zhu et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Shibamoto et al., 2019; Zhu et al., 2013).

claim: Most senescent cells in the mouse heart post-MI are cardiac myofibroblasts.
source: Most of these senescent cells are cardiac myofibroblasts, the main cell type responsible for secreting extracellular matrix components forming the scar.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Shibamoto et al., 2019; Zhu et al., 2013) in the preceding sentence.

claim: Infarction of adult constitutive p53 KO mice results in increased fibrosis and decreased inflammation in the scar 7 days post-MI.
source: Infarction of adult constitutive p53 KO mice, in which senescence induction is impeded, results in increased fibrosis and decreased inflammation in the scar 7 days post-MI (Zhu et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Zhu et al., 2013).

claim: Senescent cardiac fibroblasts limit the proliferation of non-senescent cardiac fibroblasts in a juxtacrine but not paracrine fashion in a cell culture model of isolated mouse cardiac fibroblasts.
source: In a cell culture model of isolated mouse cardiac fibroblasts, senescent cardiac fibroblasts limit the proliferation of non-senescent cardiac fibroblasts in a juxtacrine but not paracrine fashion (Shibamoto et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Shibamoto et al., 2019).

claim: Treatment of aged mice with the senolytic drug navitoclax before or after MI significantly reduces senescence burden, improves cardiac function, mitigates cardiac remodeling, and reduces scar size post-MI.
source: Treatment of aged mice with the senolytic drug navitoclax (i.e. a drug that specifically eliminates senescent cells) before or after MI significantly reduces senescence burden, improves cardiac function, mitigates cardiac remodeling, and reduces scar size post-MI, although the effects on arrhythmias has not been studied to our knowledge (Dookun et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Dookun et al., 2020).

claim: Treatment of isolated rat and mouse cardiomyocytes with exogenous SASP components including IL-6, IL-1β, and TNF-α have pro-arrhythmic effects in ion channel remodeling.
source: Indeed, treatment of isolated rat and mouse cardiomyocytes with exogenous SASP components including IL-6, IL-1β, and TNF-α have pro-arrhythmic effects in ion channel remodeling (Francis Stuart et al., 2016; Aromolaran et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Francis Stuart et al., 2016; Aromolaran et al., 2018).

claim: Aged rabbits exhibited significantly higher peri-procedural mortality compared to young rabbits (36% of aged rabbits versus 19% of young rabbits, p=0.0120).
source: Aged rabbits exhibited significantly higher peri-procedural mortality compared to young rabbits (36% of aged rabbits versus 19% of young rabbits, p=0.0120), with most young and aged peri-procedural deaths attributed to VT/VF.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the text and Figure 1A showing survival statistics.

claim: Most young and aged peri-procedural deaths were attributed to VT/VF.
source: Aged rabbits exhibited significantly higher peri-procedural mortality compared to young rabbits (36% of aged rabbits versus 19% of young rabbits, p=0.0120), with most young and aged peri-procedural deaths attributed to VT/VF.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the text and Figure 1A.

claim: There was no significant difference in SCD in the acute (3–72 hr) or chronic (≥72 hr) periods post-MI between young and aged rabbits.
source: We observed no significant difference in SCD in the acute (3–72 hr) or chronic (≥72 hr) periods post-MI between young and aged rabbits.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the text and Figure 1A.

claim: Aged rabbits exhibited a significantly higher incidence of peri-procedural lethal or nonlethal VT/VF (44% of aged rabbits versus 23% of young rabbits, p=0.0040).
source: Aged rabbits exhibited a significantly higher incidence of peri-procedural lethal or nonlethal VT/VF (44% of aged rabbits versus 23% of young rabbits, p=0.0040) (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the text and Figure 1C.

claim: Aged rabbits had a significantly decreased overall survival post-MI compared to young (p=0.0285).
source: Kaplan-Meyer analysis shows aged rabbits had a significantly decreased overall survival post-MI compared to young (p=0.0285), and all mortality of young and aged rabbits occurred within the first 48 hr post-MI (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the text and Figure 1D showing Kaplan-Meier survival curves.

claim: All mortality of young and aged rabbits occurred within the first 48 hr post-MI.
source: Kaplan-Meyer analysis shows aged rabbits had a significantly decreased overall survival post-MI compared to young (p=0.0285), and all mortality of young and aged rabbits occurred within the first 48 hr post-MI (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the text and Figure 1D.

claim: There was no significant difference in the percent infarcted area of the left ventricle between young and aged rabbits at any timepoint.
source: We found no significant difference in the percent infarcted area of the left ventricle between young and aged rabbits at any timepoint (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the text and Figure 2A.

claim: There was no significant difference in either the number or length of protrusions between young and aged rabbits at any timepoint post-MI or over time for each age group.
source: We found no significant difference in either the number or length of protrusions between young and aged rabbits at any timepoint post-MI or over time for each age group (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the text and Figure 2B.

claim: There was no difference at any timepoint between young and aged rabbits post-MI in either percent fibrotic area of the entire left ventricular free wall or in percent interstitial fibrotic area in the remote zone (RZ).
source: We observed no difference at any timepoint between young and aged rabbits post-MI in either percent fibrotic area of the entire left ventricular free wall or in percent interstitial fibrotic area in the remote zone (RZ) (Figure 2C–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the text and Figures 2C-D.

claim: In aged rabbits, APD at the IBZ was significantly longer than in the RZ (183.1±6.64 ms in IBZ and 169.4±7.90 ms in RZ, p<0.05).
source: In aged rabbits, APD at the IBZ was significantly longer than in the RZ (183.1±6.64 ms in IBZ and 169.4±7.90 ms in RZ, p<0.05), whereas in young rabbits, APD in the IBZ was significantly shorter compared to the RZ (178.9±6.99 ms in IBZ and 202.2±6.32 ms in RZ, p<0.05).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from optical mapping presented in the text and Figure 3B.

claim: In young rabbits, APD in the IBZ was significantly shorter compared to the RZ (178.9±6.99 ms in IBZ and 202.2±6.32 ms in RZ, p<0.05).
source: In aged rabbits, APD at the IBZ was significantly longer than in the RZ (183.1±6.64 ms in IBZ and 169.4±7.90 ms in RZ, p<0.05), whereas in young rabbits, APD in the IBZ was significantly shorter compared to the RZ (178.9±6.99 ms in IBZ and 202.2±6.32 ms in RZ, p<0.05).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from optical mapping presented in the text and Figure 3B.

claim: Aged rabbits exhibited greater APD heterogeneity along the IBZ compared to young rabbits.
source: Compared to young rabbits, aged rabbits exhibited greater APD heterogeneity along the IBZ (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from optical mapping presented in the text and Figure 3B.

claim: In both young and aged rabbits, conduction velocity was significantly slower in the IBZ compared to the RZ (0.32±0.10 m/s in IBZ and 0.96±0.30 m/s in RZ of aged hearts, 0.37±0.05 m/s in IBZ and 0.90±0.13 m/s in RZ of young hearts).
source: In both young and aged rabbits, conduction velocity was significantly slower in the IBZ compared to the RZ (0.32±0.10 m/s in IBZ and 0.96±0.30 m/s in RZ of aged hearts, 0.37±0.05 m/s in IBZ and 0.90±0.13 m/s in RZ of young hearts), consistent with previous findings (Mendonca Costa et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from optical mapping presented in the text and Figure 3B, and is consistent with cited literature (Mendonca Costa et al., 2018).

claim: The IBZ of aged rabbit hearts can support spatially discordant APD alternans at relatively slow heart rates.
source: We observed that the IBZ of aged rabbit hearts can support spatially discordant APD alternans at relatively slow heart rates, which has been associated with an increased risk for arrhythmias (Figure 3C; Liu et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from optical mapping presented in the text and Figure 3C, and is associated with cited literature (Liu et al., 2018).

claim: Aged rabbits exhibited significantly higher dominant VF frequency compared to young.
source: Aged rabbits exhibited significantly higher dominant VF frequency compared to young, which may be related to the underlying complexity of arrhythmia.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from optical mapping presented in the text and Figure 3D.

claim: The aged rabbit hearts displayed greater spatial variation of VF frequencies across the RZ compared to young.
source: Additionally, the aged rabbit hearts displayed greater spatial variation of VF frequencies across the RZ compared to young, whereas in young rabbits slower-frequency regions tended to cluster near the IBZ.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from optical mapping presented in the text and Figure 3D.

claim: In young rabbits slower-frequency regions tended to cluster near the IBZ.
source: Additionally, the aged rabbit hearts displayed greater spatial variation of VF frequencies across the RZ compared to young, whereas in young rabbits slower-frequency regions tended to cluster near the IBZ.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from optical mapping presented in the text and Figure 3D.

claim: In the aged rabbit scar, the percent of SA-β-gal+ cells remained elevated over time even at 12 weeks post-MI.
source: In the aged rabbit scar, the percent of SA-β-gal+ cells in the scar remained elevated over time even at 12 weeks post-MI.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from SA-β-gal staining presented in the text and Figure 4C.

claim: In the young rabbit scar, the percent of SA-β-gal+ cells was relatively high for the first 2 weeks and largely resolved by the third week post-MI, resulting in significantly decreased senescence at 3 and 12 weeks post-MI compared to aged rabbits.
source: Conversely in the young rabbit scar, the percent of SA-β-gal+ cells was relatively high for the first 2 weeks and largely resolved by the third week post-MI, resulting in significantly decreased senescence at 3 and 12 weeks post-MI compared to aged rabbits (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from SA-β-gal staining presented in the text and Figure 4C.

claim: The young and aged rabbit RZ displayed relatively very few SA-β-gal+ cells.
source: The young and aged rabbit RZ displayed relatively very few SA-β-gal+ cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from SA-β-gal staining presented in the text and Figure 4C.

claim: In young and aged sham-infarcted rabbits, low levels of SA-β-gal+ cells were observed, with no significant difference between them.
source: In the young and aged sham-infarcted rabbits, we observed low levels of SA-β-gal+ cells, with no significant difference between them (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from SA-β-gal staining presented in the text and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The percent of γH2AX+ nuclei in the aged rabbits remained elevated over time, whereas the percent of γH2AX+ nuclei in the young rabbit scar was resolved by 3 weeks post-MI, resulting in significant increases in the percent of γH2AX+ nuclei at 3 and 12 weeks post-MI in aged rabbits compared to young.
source: These results corroborated our SA-β-gal data as the percent of γH2AX+ nuclei in the aged rabbits remained elevated over time, whereas the percent of γH2AX+ nuclei in the young rabbit scar was resolved by 3 weeks post-MI, resulting in significant increases in the percent of γH2AX+ nuclei at 3 and 12 weeks post-MI in aged rabbits compared to young (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from γH2AX immunofluorescence staining presented in the text and Figure 4E.

claim: In aged rabbits 12 weeks post-MI, 9.9 ± 3% of cells were γH2AX+ whereas in young rabbits 12 weeks post-MI, only 0.6 ± 0.2% of cells were γH2AX+.
source: Specifically, in aged rabbits 12 weeks post-MI, we observed 9.9 ± 3% of cells were γH2AX whereas in young rabbits 12 weeks post-MI, only 0.6 ± 0.2% of cells were γH2AX+.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from γH2AX immunofluorescence staining presented in the text.

claim: In both the aged and young rabbit scar, initially high percentages of αSMA+ cells were observed followed by a decline over time post-MI with no significant difference between young and aged at any timepoint.
source: From our αSMA immunostaining, in both the aged and young rabbit scar, we observed initially high percentages of αSMA+ cells followed by a decline over time post-MI with no significant difference between young and aged at any timepoint (Figure 4F, left).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from αSMA immunofluorescence staining presented in the text and Figure 4F.

claim: At 2 weeks post-MI, 39.5 ± 17.5% of cells were αSMA+ in aged rabbits and 36.5 ± 8.1% of cells were αSMA+ in young rabbits.
source: At 2 weeks post-MI, 39.5 ± 17.5% of cells were αSMA+ in aged rabbits and 36.5 ± 8.1% of cells were αSMA+ in young rabbits.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from αSMA immunofluorescence staining presented in the text.

claim: The majority of γH2AX+ cells were αSMA+ at 1 week post-MI in aged and young rabbits.
source: From our double immunofluorescence staining, we observed that the majority of γH2AX+ cells were αSMA+ at 1 week post-MI in aged and young rabbits, consistent with the high levels of αSMA signal (Figure 4F, right).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from double immunofluorescence staining presented in the text and Figure 4F.

claim: At 2 weeks post-MI, ~80% of γH2AX+ cells were αSMA+.
source: Interestingly, although at 2 weeks post-MI we observed an ~50% decrease in the percent of αSMA+ cells, we observed that ~80% of γH2AX+ cells were αSMA+, indicating a propensity toward senescence of myofibroblasts.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from double immunofluorescence staining presented in the text and Figure 4F.

claim: At 2 weeks post-MI, 66.9 ± 34.3% of γH2AX+ cells were αSMA+ in aged rabbits, and 66.2 ± 45.0% of γH2AX+ cells were αSMA+ in young rabbits.
source: Specifically, at 2 weeks post-MI, 66.9 ± 34.3% of γH2AX+ cells were αSMA+ in aged rabbits, and 66.2 ± 45.0% of γH2AX+ cells were αSMA+ in young rabbits.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from double immunofluorescence staining presented in the text.

claim: Relatively few cells (~10–20%) were CD31+ at all timepoints with no significant difference between young and aged rabbits at any timepoint.
source: From our analysis of CD31 immunofluorescence staining, we observed that relatively few cells (~10–20%) were CD31+ at all timepoints with no significant difference between young and aged rabbits at any timepoint (Figure 4G, left), consistent with previous studies of cell composition post-MI (Pinto et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from CD31 immunofluorescence staining presented in the text and Figure 4G, and is consistent with cited literature (Pinto et al., 2016).

claim: At the 2 week post-MI timepoint, 12.1 ± 7.2% of cells were CD31+ in aged rabbits and 15.8 ± 11.0% of cells were CD31+ in young rabbits.
source: At the 2 week post-MI timepoint, 12.1 ± 7.2% of cells were CD31+ in aged rabbits and 15.8 ± 11.0% of cells were CD31+ in young rabbits.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from CD31 immunofluorescence staining presented in the text.

claim: Relatively few γH2AX+ cells were CD31+ across all timepoints with no significant difference between young and aged rabbits at any timepoint.
source: Similarly, we observed that relatively few γH2AX+ cells were CD31+ across all timepoints with no significant difference between young and aged rabbits at any timepoint, suggesting endothelial cells make up a minor percentage of senescent cells present in the scar post-MI (Figure 4G, right).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from double immunofluorescence staining presented in the text and Figure 4G.

claim: Two-weeks post-MI, 21.0 ± 20.1% of γH2AX+ cells were CD31+ in aged rabbits and 2.3 ± 4.5% of γH2AX+ cells were CD31+ in young rabbits.
source: Two-weeks post-MI, we observed 21.0 ± 20.1% of γH2AX+ cells were CD31+ in aged rabbits and 2.3 ± 4.5% of γH2AX+ cells were CD31+.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from double immunofluorescence staining presented in the text.

claim: In the aged scar compared to the young scar, there was a significant upregulation in the expression of all three assayed senescence genes (p16, p21, and p53), as well as the SASP components CXCL2, and TIMP2.
source: In the aged scar compared to the young scar, we observed a significant upregulation in the expression of all three assayed senescence genes (p16, p21, and p53), as well as the SASP components CXCL2, and TIMP2 (Figure 4H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from RT-qPCR presented in the text and Figure 4H.

claim: In the aged IBZ compared to the young IBZ, there was a significant upregulation in the expression of p16 and p53, as well as a significant decrease in the expression of IL-6 and CCL2.
source: In the aged IBZ compared to the young IBZ, we found a significant upregulation in the expression of p16 and p53, as well as a significant decrease in the expression of IL-6 and CCL2.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from RT-qPCR presented in the text and Figure 4H.

claim: In the aged RZ compared to the young RZ, there was a significant increase in the expression of p16 and p21, with no significant decrease in expression of any genes.
source: In the aged RZ compared to the young RZ, we found a significant increase in the expression of p16 and p21, with no significant decrease in expression of any genes.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from RT-qPCR presented in the text and Figure 4H.

claim: On average, 8 ± 5% of total cells in aged infarcted human ventricular tissue were γH2AX+.
source: On average, we observed 8 ± 5% of total cells were γH2AX+ (Figure 5B–C), and from our cell identity immunofluorescence analysis we observed an average of 61 ± 30% of cells were αSMA+, 17 ± 12% of cells were vWF+, and 21 ± 20% of cells were CD68+.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from immunofluorescence staining of human tissue presented in the text and Figures 5B-C.

claim: In aged infarcted human ventricular tissue, an average of 61 ± 30% of cells were αSMA+, 17 ± 12% of cells were vWF+, and 21 ± 20% of cells were CD68+.
source: On average, we observed 8 ± 5% of total cells were γH2AX+ (Figure 5B–C), and from our cell identity immunofluorescence analysis we observed an average of 61 ± 30% of cells were αSMA+, 17 ± 12% of cells were vWF+, and 21 ± 20% of cells were CD68+.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from immunofluorescence staining of human tissue presented in the text and Figures 5B-C.

claim: In aged infarcted human ventricular tissue, an average of 69 ± 28% of γH2AX+ cells were αSMA+, 20 ± 25% of γH2AX+ cells were vWF+, and 41 ± 17% of γH2AX+ cells were CD68+.
source: From our double immunofluorescence staining, we observed an average of 69 ± 28% of γH2AX+ cells were αSMA+, 20 ± 25% of γH2AX+ cells were vWF+, and 41 ± 17% of γH2AX+ cells were CD68+ (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from double immunofluorescence staining of human tissue presented in the text and Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Treatment with 10 µM, 20 µM, or 40 µM etoposide induced senescence in rabbit cardiac fibroblasts as measured by SA-β-gal staining.
source: For all doses of etoposide, we observed an increase in the frequency of SA-β-gal+ cells over time. Maximal SA-β-gal signal at day 12 was 73.9 ± 13.4% for the 10 μM etoposide group, 86.8 ± 4.9% for the 20 μM etoposide group, and 85.8 ± 1.8% for the 40 μM etoposide group.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from SA-β-gal staining presented in the text and Figure 6C.

claim: All proliferation of cells treated with any dose of etoposide ceased upon treatment.
source: As well described in other in vitro models, all proliferation of cells treated with any dose of etoposide ceased upon treatment (data not shown) (Campisi and Robert, 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation and is consistent with cited literature (Campisi and Robert, 2014).

claim: Cells treated with any dose of etoposide exhibited an increase in the number of γH2AX foci per nucleus over time.
source: Cells treated with any dose of etoposide exhibited an increase in the number of γH2AX foci per nucleus over time, reaching a maximum at 12 days of treatment of 19.0±9.9 γH2AX nuclear foci for the 10 μM etoposide group, 10.5±7.8 γH2AX foci for the 20 μM etoposide group, and 16.8±15.1 γH2AX foci for the 40 μM etoposide group.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from γH2AX immunofluorescence staining presented in the text and Figure 6E.

claim: After 12 days of treatment with 10 μM, 20 μM, and 40 µM etoposide, 81.7 ± 18.3%, 59.9 ± 28.1%, and 64.2 ± 42.9% of cells exhibited more than five γH2AX nuclear foci.
source: In untreated, proliferating cells, an average of 6.5 ± 7.7% of cells exhibited more than five γH2AX nuclear foci, whereas after 12 days of treatment with 10 μM, 20 μM, and 40 µM etoposide, 81.7 ± 18.3%, 59.9 ± 28.1%, and 64.2 ± 42.9% of cells exhibited more than five γH2AX nuclear foci (Figure 6F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from γH2AX immunofluorescence staining presented in the text and Figure 6F.

claim: For cells treated with 20 μM etoposide for 6 days, there was a significant increase in the expression of p16 and p21.
source: For cells treated with 20 μM etoposide for 6 days, we observed a significant increase in the expression of p16 and p21.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from RT-qPCR presented in the text and Figure 6G.

claim: For cells treated with 20 μM etoposide for 12 days, there was a significant increase in the expression of p16, p21, CXCL2, and IL-8.
source: For cells treated with 20 μM etoposide for 12 days, we observed a significant increase in the expression of p16, p21, CXCL2, and IL-8.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from RT-qPCR presented in the text and Figure 6G.

claim: There was no significant difference in IKr current between myocytes treated with proliferating-CM or SASP-CM.
source: We observed no significant difference in IKr in myocytes treated with proliferating-CM versus SASP-CM.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from patch clamp recordings presented in the text and Figure 7B.

claim: There was no significant difference between myocytes treated with proliferating-CM or SASP-CM in either APD50 or APD90.
source: We observed no significant difference between myocytes treated with proliferating-CM or SASP-CM in either APD50 or APD90, indicating that the conditioned media had no significant effect on the APD.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from patch clamp recordings presented in the text and Figure 7D.

claim: There was no significant difference in the APD between cardiomyocytes cultured with proliferating versus senescent fibroblasts, or without any fibroblasts at all.
source: Electrophysiological recordings indicated no significant difference in the APD between cardiomyocytes cultures with proliferating versus senescent fibroblasts, or without any fibroblasts at all (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from patch clamp recordings of co-cultures presented in the text and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: There was a significantly higher percentage of senescent cells neighboring IBZ myocytes in aged rabbits 3 weeks post-MI compared to young.
source: From SA-β-gal-stained frozen sections, we observed a significant increase in the percent of SA-β-gal+ cells that were adjacent to cardiomyocytes in aged rabbits compared to young (Figure 8A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from SA-β-gal staining presented in the text and Figure 8A.

claim: There was a significant increase in the average number of SA-β-gal+ cells per myocyte in aged rabbits compared to young with no difference in the number of SA-β-gal- cells per myocyte.
source: Of cells neighboring myocytes, we also observed a significant increase in the average number of SA-β-gal+ cells per myocyte in aged rabbits compared to young with no difference in the number of SA-β-gal- cells per myocyte (Figure 8B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from SA-β-gal staining presented in the text and Figure 8B.

claim: In young rabbits, the average IBZ myocyte had four neighboring non-senescent cells and in aged rabbits, the average IBZ myocyte has four neighboring non-senescent cells and one senescent cell.
source: In young rabbits, the average IBZ myocyte had four neighboring non-senescent cells and in aged rabbits, the average IBZ myocyte has four neighboring non-senescent cells and one senescent cell.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from SA-β-gal staining presented in the text.

claim: In senescent fibroblasts, Cx43 was frequently observed lining the interface between adjacent fibroblasts.
source: In senescent fibroblasts we frequently observed Cx43 lining the interface between adjacent fibroblasts, implying coupling between the cells (Figure 8C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from immunofluorescence staining presented in the text and Figure 8C.

claim: In aged rabbits, αSMA+ cells with three or more γH2AX foci were observed immediately near myocytes at the IBZ with Cx43 appearing at points of contact between the cells.
source: Particularly in aged rabbits, we observed αSMA+ cells with three or more γH2AX foci immediately near myocytes at the IBZ with Cx43 appearing at points of contact between the cells, suggesting coupling occurs in vivo (Figure 8D, Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from immunofluorescence staining presented in the text and Figure 8D, Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: In infarcted human ventricular tissue samples, αSMA+ cells with three or more γH2AX foci were observed immediately near myocytes at the IBZ with Cx43 appearing at points of contact between the cells.
source: We observed equivalent results in similarly stained infarcted human ventricular tissue samples, implying the same phenomenon occurs in human cardiac tissue (Figure 8E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from immunofluorescence staining of human tissue presented in the text and Figure 8E.

claim: In human tissue, the vast majority of apparently coupled cells were αSMA+, and nearly every coupled γH2AX+ cell was also αSMA+.
source: In human tissue, the vast majority of apparently coupled cells were αSMA+, and nearly every coupled γH2AX+ cell was also αSMA+.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from immunofluorescence staining of human tissue presented in the text and Figure 8E.

claim: Senescent myofibroblasts had a significantly larger volume compared to non-senescent ones both from frozen sections and from monolayer cultures.
source: In both cases, we observed that senescent myofibroblasts had a significantly larger volume compared to non-senescent ones, consistent with previous literature, and an overall increase in the size of in vitro myofibroblasts compared to those from tissue sections (Childs et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from volumetric measurements presented in the text and Figure 9A, and is consistent with cited literature (Childs et al., 2019).

claim: The capacitance of proliferating and senescent cardiac fibroblasts in vitro was 128.7±70.3 pF for proliferating cells and 138.4±64.0 pF for senescent cells.
source: The capacitance of proliferating and senescent cardiac fibroblasts in vitro was 128.7±70.3 pF for proliferating cells and 138.4±64.0 pF for senescent cells, and along with the volumetric measurements, we extrapolated the capacitance for proliferating and senescent rabbit cardiac fibroblasts in vivo to be 18 pF and 35 pF (see Methods), respectively (Figure 9B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from patch clamp recordings presented in the text and Figure 9B.

claim: The extrapolated capacitance for proliferating and senescent rabbit cardiac fibroblasts in vivo was 18 pF and 35 pF, respectively.
source: The capacitance of proliferating and senescent cardiac fibroblasts in vitro was 128.7±70.3 pF for proliferating cells and 138.4±64.0 pF for senescent cells, and along with the volumetric measurements, we extrapolated the capacitance for proliferating and senescent rabbit cardiac fibroblasts in vivo to be 18 pF and 35 pF (see Methods), respectively (Figure 9B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and calculations presented in the text and Figure 9B.

claim: Computational modeling showed that myocyte coupling to senescent myofibroblasts results in prolongation of APD.
source: With the extrapolated capacitance values for proliferating and senescent myofibroblasts, our modeling suggests that myocyte coupling to senescent myofibroblasts results in prolongation of APD.
evidence: The claim is supported by computational modeling data presented in the text and Figure 9C.

claim: Computational modeling showed that the aged condition resulted in a more prominent notch at phase 1 as well as a prolongation of the APD compared to young.
source: Simulating myocyte APs from young and aged tissue (Figure 9D, first panel), our modeling showed that the aged condition resulted in a more prominent notch at phase 1 as well as a prolongation of the APD compared to young (Figure 9D, second panel), consistent with our optical mapping observations of aged rabbits.
evidence: The claim is supported by computational modeling data presented in the text and Figure 9D, and is consistent with experimental optical mapping data.

claim: Computational modeling showed that the main cause of APD prolongation in the aged condition is due to the lower plateau Vm leading to a larger ICa.
source: Our modeling showed that the main cause of APD prolongation in the aged condition is due to the lower plateau Vm leading to a larger ICa (–7.4 pA/pF in the aged vs. –7.2 pA/pF in the young condition) (Figure 9D, third panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by computational modeling data presented in the text and Figure 9D.

claim: The gap junctional currents between myocyte and fibroblasts were greater in the aged condition, 8.1 pA/pF vs. 7.4 pA/pF in the young condition.
source: The gap junctional currents between myocyte and fibroblasts were greater in the aged condition, 8.1 pA/pF vs. 7.4 pA/pF in the young condition (Figure 9D, fourth panel), indicating that myocyte-fibroblast coupling causes the lower plateau Vm in the aged condition to increase ICa driving force thereby prolonging APD in the aged condition.
evidence: The claim is supported by computational modeling data presented in the text and Figure 9D.

claim: Computational modeling showed that at extrapolated capacitance values for the young and aged conditions, AP failure occurs at greater CL values under aged conditions compared to young.
source: Modeling the CL of the S2 beat at which AP failure occurred at variable values for myocyte Na channel conductance (gNa, normal = 12 mS/μF) and fibroblast capacitance (CmCF) revealed a slight decrease in the CL at onset of AP failure with increasing gNa values and an increase in the CL at onset of AP failure with increasing CmCF (Figure 9E, left). At our extrapolated capacitance values for the young and aged conditions, AP failure occurs at greater CL values under aged conditions compared to young.
evidence: The claim is supported by computational modeling data presented in the text and Figure 9E.

claim: Computational modeling showed that onset of AP failure occurred at higher CL values under aged conditions compared to young when accounting for ~73% of normal gK1 as experimentally observed in the pig IBZ.
source: Similarly, at the extrapolated values for young and aged capacitance, we found onset of AP failure occurred at higher CL values under aged conditions compared to young when accounting for ~73% of normal gK1 as experimentally observed in the pig IBZ (Hegyi et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by computational modeling data presented in the text and Figure 9E, and uses experimental data from cited literature (Hegyi et al., 2018).

claim: Coupling with senescent fibroblasts increases risks for conduction failure, heightening arrhythmogenicity in the aged MI condition.
source: These results support that coupling with senescence fibroblasts increases risks for conduction failure, heightening arrhythmogenicity in the aged MI condition.
evidence: The claim is inferred from computational modeling results presented in the text and Figure 9E.

claim: Persistence of senescent myofibroblasts is a major driver of arrhythmogenic tissue remodeling with age post-MI.
source: We propose that persistence of senescent myofibroblasts is a major driver of arrhythmogenic tissue remodeling with age post-MI, and that the timely pharmacological elimination of senescent cells might alleviate risk of arrhythmias particularly in elderly infarcted patients.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental and modeling data presented throughout the manuscript.
